newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Kucan urges ratification of EU accord.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Kucan urges ratification of EU accord.

text.p: Slovenian President Milan Kucan urged his country's parliament on Monday to ratify an association agreement with the European Union and to legislate to allow foreigners to own property as soon as possible.
"I urge (parliament) to ratify the EU association agreement immediately which is in Slovenia's vital interests...and in line with its decision to declare independence," Kucan told a news conference.

The parliament of the richest country among the ex-Yugoslav republics, which proclaimed independence in June 1991, is expected to take a vote on whether to ratify the association accord on May 14 or May 20. The accord with the EU was signed in June last year.
"I expect parliament will ratify the agreement and at the same time start procedures for a necessary change to the constitution," Kucan said.
As part of the association accord, Slovenia agreed to alter its constitution to allow foreigners to own property within four years of the association pact taking effect.
Kucan pointed out fast ratification was a precondition for Slovenia's inclusion in the first group of countries to start negotiations on full membership of the EU in 1998.
"The goal of our independence was to join international organisations, among them the EU," Kucan, the former head of Slovenia's communist party, said.
The president dismissed an attempt by a group of citizens to push for a referendum on ratification of the association agreement, which could delay the parliamentary vote.
Under Slovenian law, 40,000 signatures are needed for a referendum to be proposed. If the proposal is accepted by parliament, then the referendum must be held.
